title: Robust Site Selection and Capacity Allocation for Solar-Based Green Hydrogen: A GIS–AHP, SMAA and Optimization Approach
content: Sites for solar-based green hydrogen production are usually selected by combining geographic information systems with multi-criteria decision analysis. In this study, a GIS–analytic hierarchy process (AHP) assessment of Saudi Arabia is extended with continuous value functions, objective and hybrid weights, alternative aggregation methods, stochastic multicriteria acceptability analysis (SMAA), a levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) model, and a multi-objective allocation of the national production targets. Technical, economic, and environmental criteria are evaluated nationally and for fourteen candidate hubs, with water security and ecosystem protection treated as primary sustainability criteria. The highest suitability is found along the Red Sea coast, where Yanbu and NEOM–Oxagon are consistently ranked first and second. Its dependence on the weights is quantified by SMAA. The cost of hydrogen is governed mainly by the solar resource and the electrolyser cost, whereas suitability is governed by water access and environmental protection, and the two measures complement each other. Portfolios of hubs are identified by exact multi-objective optimization in which the average cost is lower than that of a rank-based allocation at the same level of suitability. The results provide a basis for the siting and capacity planning of the national hydrogen roadmap.
